body.purpose: Plus Jakarta Sans. Drug names, descriptions, everything read under time pressure.

label.purpose: Bottom-nav labels at 10px/700 — colour must clear AA 4.5:1 independently at that size.

mono-dose.purpose: JetBrains Mono. Numeric doses and concentrations only — the signal for "read every character".

mindmap-emphasis.purpose: Source Serif 4. Formal emphasis inside Mindmap note formatting; never in app chrome.

mindmap-heading.purpose: Space Grotesk. Headings inside Mindmap notes; never in app chrome.

shadows.name: floating-layer
shadows.purpose: The only sanctioned shadow. Dropdowns, toasts, modals, sheets — anything genuinely above the page in z-order. Resting cards never get it.

shadows.name: note-paper
shadows.purpose: Scoped exception for Mindmap board cards. One 3-slot recipe (ambient drop, contact drop, 1px edge) shared across both themes; only the third slot flips role — dark hairline in light, warm rim in dark.

shadows.name: create-tile
shadows.purpose: The "+" new-board tile. Lighter than note-paper by ratio — an unused sheet lies flatter than a pinned one — but never absent, or it goes flat among cards that have real shadows.

motion.name: ease-bounce
motion.purpose: Spring-style easing for tap confirmation and nav/tab selection. Survives prefers-reduced-motion — only decorative motion is disabled.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for colour and opacity state transitions.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Universal :active feedback via dose-press / nav-press / card-press. Applies even under reduced motion.

motion.name: pulse-scale
motion.purpose: Bounce on tab activation. Navigation and tab rows only — never a dose result or safety-tier value.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The single device-class break. Board grid drops 4 columns to 2; anchored picker panels become full-width bottom sheets.

breakpoints.name: content-max
breakpoints.purpose: Max content column for the Mindmap board wrap — lets cards grow to ~240px on desktop without spreading infinitely on ultrawide.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The committed action on a screen. Solid brand fill, pill, theme-flipped text colour.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A real action that is not the screen goal — the empty-search "Xoá bộ lọc" escape. The fill is mandatory: no border token clears 3:1 against the page.

components.name: Quiet Row Action
components.description: A repeated per-row control ("Hoàn tác" in the deleted-boards tray). Deliberately outranked by the row content: an action repeated N times must not be the brightest ink on screen.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-quiet"><svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" width="12" height="12" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M2.2 5.4h6.3a3.4 3.4 0 1 1 0 6.8H5.1" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M4.6 2.6 1.9 5.4l2.7 2.8" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.7" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>Hoàn tác</button>

components.name: Tab Chip (active / inactive)
components.description: The medication screen horizontal tab row. Active is a solid brand fill with theme-flipped text so it always clears AA.

components.name: Filter Chip with Identity Dot
components.description: Board Gallery specialty filter. One outline for the whole row; the off state keeps the specialty identity dot, lifted for dark via --c-khoa-nang.
components.css: .ds-fchips{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;row-gap:6px}.ds-fchip{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:7px;background:none;color:var(--c-text-muted,#6b6e96);border:1px solid var(--c-line,#d9ddf4);border-radius:9999px;padding:6px 12px;min-height:40px;font:600 12px/1.2 "Plus Jakarta Sans",-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:transform .18s cubic-bezier(0.34,1.4,0.64,1)}.ds-fchip-on{background:var(--c-primary,#2d3a94);color:var(--c-on-bright,#fff)}.ds-dot{width:7px;height:7px;border-radius:50%;flex-shrink:0;background:color-mix(in oklab, var(--khoa), var(--c-khoa-nang-toi,#fff) var(--c-khoa-nang,0%))}.ds-fchip:active{transform:scale(.96)}.ds-fchip:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--c-primary,#2d3a94);outline-offset:-2px}

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Palette-owned replacement for the native control — accent-color only paints the checked state, leaving an OS-grey box in dark mode. Border uses --c-text-muted because --c-line falls below the 3:1 control-boundary floor.

components.name: Search Pill
components.description: The app-wide search field. Tinted fill rather than an outline, 16px minimum font (iOS zoom guard plus the 16px Floor Rule).

components.name: Note Card (Mindmap board tile)
components.description: The signature component. A physical sheet of paper — the one sanctioned exception to the Floating-Layer-Only Rule, with a real shadow and a curled bottom-left corner. Paper does not theme-swap to dark.

components.name: Create Tile ("+" new board)
components.description: The blank sheet. Dashed border over a faint magenta wash — an owner-pinned preference (2026-08-30). The dashed border means "make a new thing" and appears nowhere else.

components.name: Bottom Navigation
components.description: Frosted tab bar. Labels always shown, never icon-only; the active pill grows in width with bounce easing.
components.html: Trang chủThư viện

components.name: Danger Severity Banner
components.description: The untouchable end of the system. Flat, serious, never animated — no bounce, glow, or celebratory motion is permitted on a danger state.

narrative.overview:
Every screen exists to answer one question fast and correctly, then get out of the way. The system is token-driven end to end — every color in the app reads from a `--c-*` CSS custom property, never a hardcoded hex — so a single palette swap recolors the entire product without touching component code. That architecture is itself a design principle: it makes the system honest about what's decoration and what's load-bearing. It's also what made this rebrand (2026-08, Deep Azure → Electric Indigo) a token-file change rather than a component-by-component rewrite.

The palette is Electric Indigo, replacing the earlier Deep Azure identity (which itself replaced an original teal). The system deliberately draws a hard line between two zones: **decoration** (navigation, tabs, cards, screen transitions) and **diagnosis** (dose numbers, safety-tier colors, warning language). Delight — spring/bounce motion, a livelier accent color — lives entirely in the first zone. The second zone is untouchable: red always means danger, amber always means caution, and neither one bounces, glows, or competes with a decorative accent for attention. This isn't timidity; it's the system's one non-negotiable rule, confirmed directly against real clinical stakes rather than assumed, and it survived the rebrand untouched — the whole reason indigo was chosen over a green/teal candidate palette was to keep the brand hue maximally distinct from all three safety hues, not just red and amber.

Night-shift use is a first-class constraint, not an afterthought: dark mode is not a lightened/darkened mirror of light mode — it's an independently authored, deliberately more dramatic identity (near-OLED-black surfaces, a luminous glow accent) so light and dark read as two confident executions of one brand rather than one screen with an inverted filter. Both are independently contrast-verified (WCAG AA, most pairs well past AAA), and a manual in-app override beats the OS preference, because clinicians often leave their phone in light mode system-wide but need this one app dark at 2am.
keyCharacteristics: Every color is a CSS custom property; there are no hardcoded hex values in components.
Danger/warning/success semantics are colorblind-safe (never color-only) and are a separate, protected token family from the primary brand color — unchanged across the 2026-08 rebrand.

Motion answers a specific question ("did my tap register," "did this number change," "did this action finish") — never pure decoration, with one exception zone (nav/tabs/cards) that now also carries brand personality.

Both light and dark mode are independently authored and contrast-verified, not generated by inverting one palette — and now deliberately *not* the same lightness relationship either (dark is darker and more saturated-glow than a simple light-mode inversion would produce).

rules.name: The One Other Place Rule
rules.body: This color appears nowhere outside the Mindmap board — not in the dosing screens, not in navigation — specifically so it never competes with the hazard-signal palette for visual priority. Unchanged by the 2026-08 rebrand.

rules.name: The Untouchable Signal Rule
rules.body: `--c-danger*`, `--c-warn*`, and `--c-green*` are a separate token family from `--c-primary*`/`--c-accent*` and are never restyled, retinted, or animated as part of a brand refresh — confirmed by surviving the 2026-08 Azure→Indigo rebrand completely unchanged, byte-for-byte. Red is always danger, amber is always caution, and neither one gets the bounce/pop/glow treatment the rest of the UI uses for delight — a flat, serious presentation at the exact moment a clinician needs to trust the color without a second thought. **Favorite Gold (`--c-fav`) is not part of this family** and not a signal — it is a scoped decorative accent (see above), kept chromatically distinct from clinical amber on purpose.

rules.name: The Decoration/Diagnosis Split Rule
rules.body: Delight (spring motion, brand color, glow, playful entrance animation) is scoped to navigation, tabs, cards, and screen transitions. Dose numbers, calculated results, and safety-tier text are typographically and chromatically calm by comparison — the loudest thing on a dosing screen is always the danger signal, never the brand. A calm "ok" dose result reads in `--c-text`, not `--c-primary` — brand color is chrome, not a stamp of approval on a clinical number.

rules.name: The 16px Floor Rule
rules.body: No input, textarea, or select ever renders below 16px, without exception — this is an accessibility fix (prevents unwanted iOS zoom) and a safety fix (dose entry text is never allowed to be small) enforced by the same line of CSS.

rules.name: The Floating-Layer-Only Rule
rules.body: `box-shadow` (and, in dark mode, the glow halo) appears only on elements that are genuinely elevated above the page in z-order (dropdowns, toasts, modals, sheets). A card at rest never has a shadow or a glow; if something needs one to look important, it should have moved into a floating layer instead.

dos: **Do** read every color from a `--c-*` CSS custom property — a hardcoded hex anywhere in a component is a bug, not a style choice.
**Do** keep `--c-danger*`, `--c-warn*`, and `--c-green*` completely independent of the primary/accent palette, including through any future rebrand.
**Do** verify new color pairs against WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text, higher for small label text) before shipping them, the way every existing token was verified.
**Do** keep tap-confirmation motion (`:active` scale) working even under `prefers-reduced-motion`; only decorative motion should respect that media query.
**Do** scope new delight/motion/glow additions to navigation, tabs, cards, and transitions — never to dose numbers or safety-tier text.
**Do** let dark mode be a *deliberately distinct* execution of the brand (deeper, more saturated-glow) rather than a mechanical inversion of light mode.

**Do** count how many times an accent color appears on one screen before shipping it. Used once it is emphasis; repeated per row it becomes the body color and quietly outranks the content it decorates.
**Do** give a secondary action a real fill (`button-secondary`), not an outline alone — no border token in this system clears 3:1 against the page.
donts: **Don't** add bounce, pop, glow, or celebratory motion to a danger or warning state, ever — this is the system's one hard line, confirmed directly against clinical risk rather than a generic accessibility guess.
**Don't** use the Mindmap-only magenta accent (`--c-accent-2`) anywhere in the medication or dosing screens.
**Don't** let any input, textarea, or select render below 16px font size.
**Don't** invert one theme to produce the other — light and dark are both independently authored and contrast-checked.
**Don't** let brand color (`--c-primary`) sit on a calm/"ok" clinical result — reserve it for chrome, navigation, and actions; a normal dose reads in `--c-text`.

**Don't** place a decorative accent immediately beside a hazard signal. Measure it: magenta `#f175a6` next to danger `#ff8585` is ΔE(CIE76) 26 at 4px apart — close enough to read as "two pinks" on a permanent-delete control. In any bulk-action strip, the destructive action is the *only* colored one.

**Don't** dress a non-create action in the paper material (`.mind-o-tao-bang`) or a dashed border. Both mean "make a new thing"; a reset, filter, or dismiss control wearing either is lying about what it does.
**Don't** hand a control's outline the divider token (`--c-line`). Dividers may sit near 1.3:1; a control boundary owes 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) and needs `--c-text-muted` or stronger.
